**<sub><sub>![P2 Badge](https://img.shields.io/badge/P2-yellow?style=flat)</sub></sub>  Ignore capture loss after a completed pointerup**

This is the fixed historical **46fa65bb → 4a232076** comparison, not latest main or #847. Median first-click→input was 32.1→71.6 ms early and 31.2→68.7 ms settled. This Draft remains evidence-only and **must never merge**.

The full historical report is reproduced below under the owner's publication authorization. In the preserved report, “current main/current” means only `4a2320762ba5f4319dec1915ca4e138772dceb0c` at measurement time; the proposal and #816 status are historical. # Search cold-open before/after measurement

Observed 2026-10-05 17:31–17:35 UTC. Evidence-only [Draft PR #846](https://github.com/Proto-UI/Proto-UI/pull/846), never merge. No product implementation or original 1000 ms opener acceptance was changed.

## Result

This bounded whole-tree comparison measured a roughly 37–40 ms higher median first-click-to-input interval on current main under the isolated conditions below. It does not establish that the whole site regressed, that the original opener gate failed, or that one migration alone caused every observed delta. All 40 natural samples, two HEAD503 controls and two separately profiled samples completed with actual Button documentation results, no missing observations and no page errors.

The migration changed where Pagefind preparation occurs: all 20 baseline natural samples completed HEAD + GET for the same pagefind.js before the first click; all 20 current samples had neither before that click. These are two requests, not two modules or a fully preloaded search index. Metadata/WASM/index loading remained later. Both actual Pagefind runtime files had identical SHA-256 bytes.

## Source and execution binding

- Baseline: `46fa65bb0146d951a08f6368ee4568be57fba3f5`, the only parent of Search migration `8a49c6b7bc3777d682a08ee6f0e0fcda5bf87cbe`. Its direct Search diff removes DCL/idle ensureSearchReady and adds lazy ownership. This is the exact immediate migration boundary, not an arbitrary old release.
- Current main: `4a2320762ba5f4319dec1915ca4e138772dceb0c`. PR #816 remained open at `d6bf13e18dabb6cab223eda2c81d99666baa5930`; no claim is made about that candidate's elapsed performance.
- Probe: `82dab2249da23ef222d335125f519b90849e9e4a`, independently reviewed before publication. Six negative-control tests passed locally and on CI. An initial invisible staging-opener measurement flaw was repaired and tested before the run; no earlier fabricated performance result exists.
- [Run 37349035229](https://github.com/Proto-UI/Proto-UI/actions/runs/37349035229), job 111894894825: success. Exactly two production builds, serial, both tracked-source-clean; one added measurement job. Other repository PR CI runs independently and is not this result.
- Chrome `154.0.8037.57`, Node `v24.21.0`, Ubuntu 24.04 runner. Same `/zh-cn/ui-libraries/shadcn/button/`, 1440×960, light theme, WC preference. Current actual Search runtime was asserted WC; baseline uses its native Search commands.
- Fresh context per sample; HTTP cache disabled and service workers blocked on both. Same-page second open retains Pagefind instance/module memory. No network/CPU throttle; local static production origin. This is not a cold browser-process or OS-cache test.
- Source order alternated, n=10/source/timing cohort. The earliest automated cohort clicks after DCL and Playwright actionability, not guaranteed before idle work. Actual early clicks: baseline DCL+484.5–767.1 ms; current DCL+378.4–462.4 ms. Baseline was already prewarmed in every early sample. Settled clicks occurred after DCL+2 s on both.

## Natural latency distributions

Milliseconds, nearest-rank median and p90, no imputation. Raw values are in `natural-samples.csv` and the original per-sample JSON. Every row has n=10, zero failed/missing samples.

| Cohort | Metric | Baseline min / median / p90 / max | Current min / median / p90 / max |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| early | First click → visible enabled focused input | 31.3 / 32.1 / 42.0 / 48.6 | 66.8 / 71.6 / 76.0 / 96.0 |
| early | Button input → visible semantic result | 320.6 / 328.6 / 364.8 / 404.3 | 328.8 / 345.9 / 366.4 / 367.2 |
| early | Second click → input | 17.6 / 18.6 / 19.8 / 20.1 | 24.2 / 26.5 / 28.0 / 28.0 |
| settled | First click → visible enabled focused input | 30.4 / 31.2 / 32.2 / 32.6 | 66.5 / 68.7 / 70.7 / 73.9 |
| settled | Button input → visible semantic result | 321.1 / 322.1 / 353.5 / 361.5 | 329.8 / 348.9 / 364.5 / 365.6 |
| settled | Second click → input | 17.3 / 18.7 / 19.7 / 20.8 | 24.5 / 24.8 / 25.3 / 27.0 |

Pre-click **all-page** long-task duration sums had medians 407→498 ms (early) and 350→517 ms (settled), with raw values retained in the CSV. These are whole-page tasks above the long-task threshold, not total CPU work and not Search-attributed work. This run therefore does not establish a compensating startup saving from the lazy policy.

The first-open median differences are +39.5 ms (early) and +37.5 ms (settled). Query differences are +17.3/+26.8 ms and reopen differences +7.9/+6.1 ms. These are differences of descriptive medians, not paired causal estimates, percentage speedups or new budgets. The query interval includes Pagefind default UI's 300 ms debounce; it is not CPU-only search time.

Opener-ready timestamps from navigation are recorded in summary.json as a separate descriptive metric. They have a different time origin and predicate from the existing stage-anchored 1000 ms test. A value around/above 1000 here cannot be called that test's failure or pass.

## What the two diagnostic traces add

These are one settled profile per source, excluded from distributions. `trace-decomposition.json` aligns the main document navigationStart with page performance.now timestamps and clips main-renderer X events to each interval. It takes unions within a category rather than summing nested entries. Category totals, callbacks, network durations and background-worker time overlap and must not be added together. This is a timeline capture, not CPU sampling or a source-map-resolved profiler; complete streamed JSON was received, but trace data-loss certification was not collected.

- First click→input: baseline 33.3 ms; current 71.6 ms. The initial outer click EventDispatch is 31.29 ms versus 27.55 ms. Main-thread style/layout/prepaint/paint-related event union is 30.30 versus 33.44 ms. This does not show a new 38 ms Button mount. Search still has native dialog + Pagefind UI; only open/close/retry commands are prototype Buttons. No nonexistent Dialog prototype cost is assigned.
- Current first open: HEAD begins +24.0 ms and lasts 7.6 ms; pagefind.js GET starts +33.9 ms and lasts 3.9 ms; default UI ui-core starts +42.5 ms and lasts 3.3 ms. Those modules are ready for subsequent initialization before input is observed at +71.6 ms. Baseline corresponding module work happened approximately 1.52 s before click.
- Current named background parse events: pagefind.js at +38.395 ms for 1.414 ms; ui-core at +46.294 ms for 2.267 ms. Main-thread compile-module entries are 0.019/0.029 ms. Anonymous module-evaluation spans around +40.2/+49.1 ms last 1.726/0.217 ms; URL-less spans are not independently source-attributed CPU samples. Remaining post-download interval includes UI construction, DOM/style/layout/focus, scheduling and rAF observation, not a pure parse cost.
- Query: style/layout/paint union 13.40→21.00 ms within 357.9→363.7 ms trace intervals. Current callbacks include SiteCopyBootstrap and site-typography-client, but inclusive callback durations and broad whole-tree differences do not prove either causes the median query delta. Pagefind metadata and index differ between source trees.
- Reopen: 19.0→29.4 ms; style/layout/paint union 17.31→20.64 ms. Current command-dispatch callback encloses about 19.66 ms and native style/layout work; that is not exclusive JavaScript or isolated Button overhead.

Raw resource records and trace callsite/event data are retained for further attribution. The rAF observer itself introduces equal-purpose, but not zero, diagnostic overhead and frame-quantized observation latency.

## Failures, retries and visual evidence

Both separately labelled HEAD503 controls observed the real failure UI, a failed HEAD, one actual retry click, a successful HEAD, query results and a second open. Retry-click→input was 76.1 ms baseline and 73.4 ms current in these single injected controls. Neither enters the natural distribution. They are not retry-performance equivalence estimates.

`final.png` captures the second open after Escape, when Pagefind has cleared the query, not the result list. The semantic result evidence is each sample's matching same-origin Button links and result timestamp. Both runner screenshots lack CJK glyphs (boxes); these are real state captures but not Chinese typography or visual-parity approval. Four representative images (both reopened and both HEAD503) were inspected.

## Important limitations

The browser applied the same no-external-network rule, but the baseline attempted four esm.sh framework requests per sample (React/ReactDOM/Vue2/Vue3), all blocked, while current attempted none. This asymmetric response is part of the old/new page source and a confound. Results do not represent the unrestricted deployed site or isolate only Search. Both lockfiles, HTML and generated index metadata differ. Resource requests blocked for isolation were retained; no credentials or private user page content were used.

One route, family, viewport, theme, runtime and query; n=10/cohort on one runner. No physical mobile, arbitrary queries, warm HTTP-cache, slow network or CPU-throttle matrix. Missing CJK fonts and isolated runtime-fetch behavior further bound generalization. A green capture means complete evidence, not total performance parity. No product defect or merge blocker is created from this result alone.

## Smallest evidence-backed next option (proposal only)

Prefer evaluating **module-only preparation on deliberate Search intent** (pointer intent or keyboard focus) before considering unconditional idle initialization. Reuse a single service-owned preparation promise for HEAD/runtime/default-UI import; leave Pagefind instance/DOM construction and dialog opening to the actual open. Preserve runtime-switch ownership, disconnect cleanup, retry reset, error handling and immediate keyboard opening when no prior intent exists. Do not move a full hidden Pagefind subtree and its style work onto critical page startup.

An optional late-idle module preparation policy needs its own page-startup/unused-work budget and source-matched validation; this trace does not justify simply restoring old idle ensureSearchReady. Keyboard shortcut/direct-touch opens may receive no preparation lead, so any benefit must be scoped to the measured intent cases.

A subsequent product trial should use the same fixed current application source with only that bounded change, preserve the existing opener 1000 ms acceptance unchanged, and separately measure (a) no-intent page load/opener, (b) intent→open with actual preparation lead, (c) immediate open/no lead, (d) first results and second open, and (e) HEAD503/retry, close during prepare, repeated intent/click and disposal. Compare raw distributions and source-bound pre-click bytes/long tasks; require no lost readiness, duplicate requests, stale focus or error/retry behavior. Do not accept a first-open improvement that merely worsens startup or unused work without an explicit product trade-off. No optimization code was written in this measurement task.

## Raw evidence and preservation

[Original Actions artifact 11360959718](https://github.com/Proto-UI/Proto-UI/actions/runs/37349035229/artifacts/11360959718), 2,844,729 bytes; ZIP SHA-256 `75119b35d07f3220714d262d0af97059615171d9c7cbbbc7093d7079760a681c`. Actions retention is 14 days, so the downloaded original ZIP must accompany the durable work handoff rather than treating the hosted URL as permanent storage.

Original inventory: boundary.json, summary.json, two build logs, browser.txt, run.log; 40 natural per-sample JSON files; two HEAD503 per-sample JSON files and failure/reopen captures; two trace sample JSON files, trace.json and final captures. `evidence-manifest.json` enumerates every local original and derived file with SHA-256. Derived material: this report, natural-samples.csv, trace-decomposition.json/.txt; no original record was modified. Independent artifact review recomputed every summary distribution and all per-sample time differences and confirmed 44/44 validity.

## Deprecated-pattern audit: tracked Select ownership residue and integration candidate

Sanitized maintainer request: check whether patterns already marked unused/deprecated—especially early Agent A/B control implementations—survive without a current purpose; track confirmed residue and address it in this Finf PR.

### Bounded audit disposition

The audit covered main `ca28a4db278f948e34c57ae779385673d37d391b` and the relevant Finf sources through `48b6f1bf6def5ffe1d1a7c34be91d670b1e7a077`. It did **not** establish a distinct abandoned-production-control defect. The Liquid `source-157-control` remains an explicit same-scene comparison oracle; the reviewed build/browser paths still exercise baseline and candidate. Material V1/V2 ownership and Presence retention still have explicit boundaries/decision gates, so their presence alone does not authorize deletion. This is not a repository-wide clean bill of health.

One actionable deprecated consumer is already tracked by **#637**, including its existing Select migration decision. No duplicate Issue was created, and #637 is not resolved by this one consumer change.

### Ready source candidate for the Finf integrator

Commit: [`9737c1a8c7f89df44610022861f58706ad388592`](https://github.com/Proto-UI/Proto-UI/commit/9737c1a8c7f89df44610022861f58706ad388592)

Branch: `audit/state-accessor-select-20261009`; parent: `48b6f1bf6def5ffe1d1a7c34be91d670b1e7a077`.

Exactly two files:
- `packages/prototypes/base/src/select/item.proto.ts`: replace `def.state.fromAccessibility('selected')` with Select-owned `def.state.bool('selected', false)`.
- `packages/prototypes/base/test/select.test.ts`: preserve a consumer-observable coexistence regression, including controlled Root updates and conflicting writes through the retained legacy slot.

Authority: active `D-STATE-SEMANTIC-ACCESSORS-DEPRECATION-0001` and the draft `P-BASE-SELECT-ITEM` state-separation/controlled/a11y rules. No lifecycle promotion, public API/export change, Runtime accessor removal, invented Tooltip press semantics, or Presence retirement.

### Actual reproduction and verification

With controlled Root value `alpha` and Item value `beta`, a composed consumer writes the existing borrowed accessibility slot to `true` through an exposed method:

| Observation | Before | After |
| --- | --- | --- |
| Root value | `alpha` | `alpha` |
| Item protocol `selected` | incorrectly becomes `true` | remains `false` |
| Item `aria-selected` | incorrectly becomes `true` | remains `false` |

The identical real WC Adapter/Runtime/Base smoke scenario failed before and passed after. Changing the owning Root value to `beta` still selects the Item; a later borrowed-slot `false` cannot clear that legitimate selection.

- Focused Select matrix: **9 files, 88/88 tests passed** across Base, Shadcn, Brutalist, Liquid Material, the four-family projection harness, React/React keyboard, Vue and Vue 2.
- Workspace TypeScript: `tsc -p tsconfig.workspace.json --noEmit` passed on Node 24.21.0.
- Initial collection/type-check failures from missing declared dependency links/generated prerequisites were retained. The same checks passed after restoring declared cached dependencies and using the canonical CLI/style generator; no manifest, lockfile, type-check exclusion or assertion was weakened.

These are HappyDOM/fake-clock ownership and integration observations, **not native-browser visual evidence**. No new native visual acceptance, hosted CI result, independent review, or whole-Finf acceptance is claimed. Existing normative/public documentation already describes the intended ownership and was intentionally unchanged.

### Integration boundary

At handoff preflight, #872 head was `342955e238e6a632dbc010b70aa59d1a373ce440`. Its eight-commit delta from the candidate's parent changes neither of these two files. This candidate was published only to its separate branch; the Finf integration ref was not written.

Please have the Finf integrator independently review and incorporate this exact commit under its current expected-head boundary, then rerun affected checks on the actual combined head. The repair remains **pending Finf integration/acceptance**; no delivery checkbox is marked complete and no Issue is closed by this handoff.

## Commit progress — `f288a07cd3394f5f0bc61d9b497583534ce19916`

User-request paraphrase: advance the existing private-input/retest repair through ordinary contributor publication, real CI, independent review and rule-compliant integration. This report does not authorize or claim a bypass.

### Change and owning boundary

Normal main synchronization retains both original parents `1b51763db6669ac3cba7e7f9f1a6cb89a9e3eba4` and `7e28d06f26150513d6096f0c24e59b871ae8ae62`; candidate tree `f6a5e5f6364ec578f36e0afcf78f6afed9309d8a`. The PR retains its nine-file AgentOps privacy/retest slice; existing main material/type/website changes are not new work attributed to this commit.

Review submission/merge and collaboration apply now admit both private record/context paths after independent mode/source validation and before owner-proof or task-artifact reads. The independent audit exposed an additional deterministic alias: a raw record reused as `--handoff`, or a raw context reused as an owner key, was opened through an earlier `readFileSync` even though the dedicated loader later had a containment guard. Native reproduction observed those raw reads before the source correction. The corrected ordering rejects them before either raw input is opened. Read-only collaboration validation stays measurement-free; no-follow bounded reads, recomputation, freshness, scope and real write authorization remain separate checks. Realpath observation is not an atomic filesystem sandbox.

The retained retest rule rejects `retest-inconsistent` without a prior digest in both runtime and receipt schema. Linked consistent retests do not require that anomaly, and a digest is not authenticated prior/model identity.

### Executed evidence

- Identical retained consumers on actual main: **105/111 passed, six expected failures**; pre-alias synchronized candidate: **111/111 passed**.
- Strengthened handoff/owner-key alias controls on unchanged pre-fix production: **64/68 passed, four failures**, with actual raw-path read observations and no external call. Corrected complete focused set: **113/113 passed** across ModelTrace and both invocation suites.
- Affected owner/review/collaboration authorization controls, serialized: **227/227 passed**. These are local synthetic/temporary-Git controls, not a real GitHub approval or merge.
- AgentOps source and lazy-skill checks passed (**42 skills, 40 lazy leaves**); disposable snapshot generated from **687 entities**; post-generator Agent docs and nine-file Prettier checks passed.
- Fresh independent read-only admission and evidence audits found no remaining in-scope findings. They performed no execution or external write and are not platform `APPROVED` reviews.

### Honest remaining gates

The complete default-concurrency AgentOps command hit the unchanged **240-second** bound (603 passes/32 cancellations, not a complete green aggregate). A controlled run retaining all files/assertions with concurrency 2 also timed out at the same bound. Neither timeout is relabelled as passing; the narrower 113+227 evidence does not replace the full aggregate. The precise source/resource cause remains unestablished, and no deadline/assertion/selection/policy change was made to hide the debt.

New exact-head hosted CI, independent platform approval and repository rules remain integration gates. `guangliang2019` was already requested; no duplicate request, self-approval, CI rerun/cancellation, force push, merge bypass or Issue closure is claimed. Issues #469 and #687 remain untouched. No scorer/bank/count/tolerance/schemaVersion/policy/TTL/numeric-budget/credential/settings or product-lifecycle changes.

## Agent evidence — actual intranet cutover and legacy retirement

**Request paraphrase (Agent):** retire the Poppy-only preview system completely, keep one intranet preview implementation, and preserve unrelated bot, identity, admin and review-broker capabilities. This is a factual progress report, not merge approval or Issue closure.

### Exact source and delivery

- Candidate head: `1699b70ecf5ff51459aebb3f7bedeed92f9f111b`; reviewed baseline: `ea19727838d85c05af5e4bca8d5fc235cb44e288`.
- Commit `f8eda9c295130dc76a440d80570071542e03dec3` removes the old workflows, duplicate integration package, Cloudflare provider, private-handler contract, report/upload and sticky-comment paths; the single bounded admission/extraction authority moves to `scripts/preview` without aliases.
- Commit `1699b70ecf5ff51459aebb3f7bedeed92f9f111b` fixes old manual-run discovery and read-quota exhaustion: complete discovery is bounded, cached facts are negative only, new attempts invalidate them, and no cache grants Ready admission.
- The [actual secret-free hosted build](https://github.com/Proto-UI/Proto-UI/actions/runs/38026117154) succeeded at this exact head. Artifact `11660565184`, attempt `1`, was admitted against the still-open PR and deployed on the one intranet origin family. Private host addresses, access data and screenshots containing unrelated data are not published here.

### Exercised native boundaries

- The real intranet catalog, generation page and local assets load. Homepage → Libraries → Base Input was navigated in Chromium 150, English/light, 1440×1080, DPR 1.25.
- Native pointer/keyboard entry and readonly focus/non-editing were exercised in Web Component, React, Vue and Vue 2. No DOM-value or CSS injection; no OS IME, all-browser, all-component or native-host conformance claim. The unstyled Base WC input clips long displayed text at its intrinsic width; the full DOM value was verified, not represented as width parity.
- GET/HEAD serving, directory redirect `308`, foreign-host `404`, noncurrent-generation `410`, Worker request `403`, and non-GET/HEAD `405` were observed on the real entry. This HTTP entry is **not** a secure context; secure-context-only APIs are not claimed.
- The dedicated static identity actually reads the site, cannot write the site/catalog and cannot read the publisher's private GitHub credentials. Hosted contributor code does not execute on the persistent privileged publisher.
- The real two-minute publication timer was paused for a failure-path observation. After the unchanged five-minute lease expired, both catalog and generation returned `503`; the timer was restored and both returned `200`. Repeated native syncs reacquired the same regular-file kernel lock. Forced termination and reboot were not exercised.
- Final native preview suite: **61/61**. Affected collector suite: **167/167** after repairing only the ignored local locked dependency availability; the initial missing-dependency failure remains retained. No full-workspace pass is inferred from these focused results.

### Legacy Actions retirement performed

All five exact old workflow registrations now read back as `disabled_manually`: bootstrap `341174527`, build `340871813`, cleanup `341174528`, deploy `341174529`, security `340993769`. Only the three previously active registrations were mutated; the two already disabled entries were no-ops. Complete current inventories found no old runs in in_progress, queued, waiting, requested or pending states. Historical failed runs were neither erased nor rerun.

Only repository-level `POPPY_PREVIEW_EDGE_SECRET` and `POPPY_PREVIEW_INGEST_SECRET` were removed, and absence was read back. No secret value was read. Generic `CLOUDFLARE_ACCOUNT_ID` and `CLOUDFLARE_API_TOKEN` metadata stayed unchanged; shared origin, OAuth, webhook, broker and organization/environment credentials are not claimed retired.

### Coverage and outstanding debt — partial

1. Four exact-head native Input PNGs are captured and visually inspected, but **not uploaded**. The managed GitHub attachment surface is unauthenticated. Upload URLs and public visual evidence remain debt; local captures are not uploads, and no new Release/storage surface or fabricated URL was created.
2. The companion bot/edge removal is locally verified, including seven retired HTTP routes returning `404` with surviving health/readiness/admin behavior. That is not production deployment evidence. The deployed shared bot/edge revision, ownership-bound old Pages project/domain cleanup and exact obsolete App callback registration still need authorized management readback. Shared parent services/App/database are explicitly excluded from deletion.
3. [Ordinary CI run 38026117117](https://github.com/Proto-UI/Proto-UI/actions/runs/38026117117) **failed** in general and browser suites. Its runner checkout is merge `47966b5bc15745174a457246859203380da14a6a` of this head into the named baseline. Owning errors are under bounded diagnosis; the successful intranet build/checks do not replace this failed evidence.
4. The legacy security run's earlier missing private-handler token failure is preserved. Retiring its obsolete workflow is not a passing security result. Independent exact-head review and normal integration gates remain open; no self-approval or merge occurred, and #612 is not closed by this report.

The shared Drawer Trigger and Close command advertises `activate -> click`, but both behaviors are implemented only by their separate `press.commit` listeners. **<sub><sub>![P2 Badge](https://img.shields.io/badge/P2-yellow?style=flat)</sub></sub>  Route Popover commands through accessible activation**

Popover Trigger and Close commands advertise `activate -> click`, but their open/close requests are implemented only by `press.commit`; this shared command handles neither `click` nor activation. Native assistive-technology activation therefore cannot open or close the Popover, so route the semantic event through each command's existing guarded operation.

**<sub><sub>![P2 Badge](https://img.shields.io/badge/P2-yellow?style=flat)</sub></sub>  Expose Number Field adjustment actions**

The input publishes a `spinbutton` role and complete range state, but declares neither `increment` nor `decrement`; changing the value is available only through physical keyboard input or separate visible buttons. Native screen-reader adjustment gestures therefore cannot operate the focused spinbutton, so map both semantic actions to the existing `stepBy` path while preserving disabled and readOnly guards.

fullNativeSourceMetadata.body:
**<sub><sub>![P2 Badge](https://img.shields.io/badge/P2-yellow?style=flat)</sub></sub>  Emit accepted controlled OTP completion**

When a controlled OTP proposes a full-length code, `value` still contains the owner's previous value, so this equality condition suppresses `completed`; when the owner later accepts the proposal through props, the sync path updates `complete` but never emits the event. Controlled consumers therefore never receive `completed`, so detect the accepted complete transition during owner synchronization or track the proposal until its owner echo.

**<sub><sub>![P1 Badge](https://img.shields.io/badge/P1-orange?style=flat)</sub></sub>  Scope manual-run supersession to its bound PR**

When any newer `workflow_dispatch` run exists—even one whose binding marker targets another PR—this predicate removes every older Ready row from `current.json` before that marker is resolved. Because the unrelated manual run remains in the discovered history, unaffected previews return 410 throughout every subsequent synchronization, potentially for most of the four-minute scan window; resolve the marker first and revoke only the PR it actually supersedes, as the final admission path already does.

**<sub><sub>![P2 Badge](https://img.shields.io/badge/P2-yellow?style=flat)</sub></sub>  Keep the last synchronization error until a retry succeeds**

When `current.json` contains the error from a previous failed synchronization, this intermediate rewrite omits that error before per-PR admission and the final live-head scan have succeeded. During every retry, the server therefore reports a healthy empty catalog with 200/410 responses instead of the documented 503—potentially for most of the four-minute scan—even when the retry later fails and the outer catch restores the error; preserve the error state until the successful final manifest replacement.

**<sub><sub>![P1 Badge](https://img.shields.io/badge/P1-orange?style=flat)</sub></sub>  Bind empty-association runs to the marker's PR**

When two open PRs share the same head repository, ref, and SHA—for example, when one head targets two different base branches—an Actions run whose `pull_requests` array is empty satisfies this fallback for both catalog rows. A queued or failed run then assigns the wrong lifecycle directly, while a successful run resolves the first PR's marker and is still assigned to the second row because `binding.pr` is never compared with `row.pr`; use the immutable binding marker to disambiguate the PR before assigning any status or generation.

finalPostmergeRecords.body:
**<sub><sub>![P1 Badge](https://img.shields.io/badge/P1-orange?style=flat)</sub></sub>  Exclude failed samples from latency distributions**

When a sample fails after recording an earlier metric—for example, `openToInputMs` succeeds but the query or reopen stage times out—this mapping still feeds that finite value into the cohort distribution. Because `summary.json` is written before the final all-samples-complete assertion and artifacts are uploaded even on failure, a red run can report partial failed attempts as valid observations and skew its median/p90 despite listing the sample under `failed`; substitute `null` for every metric unless `s.status === 'complete'`.

finalPostmergeRecords.body:
**<sub><sub>![P2 Badge](https://img.shields.io/badge/P2-yellow?style=flat)</sub></sub>  Retain the generated Pagefind corpus in the build boundary**

The query timing is measured against generated `.pf_index`, metadata, and fragment files, but the boundary hashes only the route HTML and `pagefind.js`; the workflow also uploads only the runner-temp report directory, so the actual generated corpus and default-UI asset used by the run are discarded. This matters here because the two revisions intentionally have different generated corpora and those generated bytes can vary independently of the runtime hash, leaving an anomalous `queryToResultMs` distribution impossible to audit or reproduce from the retained artifact; record a manifest of the complete Pagefind/UI inputs or copy them into the artifact.
